clue.text: Computerised woollies, say

parts.note: woollies are soft things to put on, so 'computerised' clothing of that kind suggests the programs a machine runs, with WARE heard in 'wear'

explanation.surface: A gadget-mad knitter has put chips in the jumpers.
explanation.walkthrough: Woollies (woolly jumpers, cardigans) are soft wear; the computing word for programs is spelt with WARE, which says the same as 'wear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Programs run by computers are called by this name, as opposed to the physical machinery.

clue.text: Discharged one's assets in flight?

parts.note: selling off everything one owns, perhaps before fleeing, or while rising up as in flight

explanation.surface: Someone liquidated everything before running off abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests escape, but it also hints at going upward, matching the second word of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has sold all their goods or business has disposed of everything for cash.

clue.text: But he sounds a more distant relative

indicators.note: sounds signals that a word is said aloud rather than spelt

explanation.surface: A remark that a man is even more remotely related than thought.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech FARTHER (more distant) is said like the word for a male parent; 'But he' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A male parent is a close family member.

clue.text: Something to examine from time to time

definitions.text: Something to examine from time to time

parts.words: Something to examine from time to time
parts.note: a device you glance at periodically to learn the hour; to examine is also to observe

explanation.surface: Sounds like something you inspect occasionally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From time to time' looks like 'occasionally', but you look at this to find the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrist timepiece is consulted to learn the hour, and the verb means to observe.

clue.text: Travel discount for one on a diet?

definitions.meaning: a cheaper ticket price for travel
a dieter eats less, so their food is cut down

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a cheaper ticket, and also describes the cut-down food of a slimmer.

clue.text: Outsize flag for an Egyptian god

parts.note: OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize
the yellow flag is a wild iris, so flag can mean iris

explanation.surface: An enormous banner has been run up to honour a deity of the Nile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner, but it is the plant: the yellow flag is a species of iris.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the Egyptian ruler of the underworld, husband of Isis.

clue.text: Tasty offering a bit near the bone, perhaps

definitions.text: Tasty offering a bit near the bone, perhaps

parts.words: Tasty offering a bit near the bone, perhaps
parts.note: a sugary delicacy, read also as the sweetest flesh, said to lie nearest the bone

explanation.surface: Sounds like a slightly risque joke being served up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near the bone' usually means risque; the saying 'the nearer the bone, the sweeter the meat' gives the reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A confection or candied delicacy, its old name containing the word for flesh.

clue.text: Evaluated as a tax open to criticism?

definitions.meaning: liable to local property tax assessment
to rate can mean to scold or berate, so one who may be scolded

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes property assessed for local taxes, and literally one who can be scolded, from the old verb 'rate'.

clue.text: Looking embarrassed in a woolly coat?

definitions.meaning: like a ram or ewe in its fleece

explanation.definitionFit: The word means shamefaced, and literally means resembling the woolly farm animal.

clue.text: Freedom of choice in the cartography line

definitions.meaning: scope or leeway to act as one pleases
a parallel drawn east-west on maps, measuring distance from the equator

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both leeway to act as one wishes and the mapmaker's parallel north or south of the equator.

clue.text: Biggest draw at Wimbledon

parts.note: the main show arena at the tennis championships, where the top matches pull the largest crowds

explanation.surface: Asking which match or player pulls the largest crowd at the tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests the tournament draw, but here it means attraction: the main show stage of the All England Club in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal show arena at the All England Club hosts the headline matches and attracts the largest audiences.

clue.text: Penny's place found in auctioneer's lot

indicators.note: found in shows the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A coin turns up in a batch of goods put up for auction.
explanation.walkthrough: The run crosses the word break: auctioneeR'S LOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin-operated machine has a narrow opening where the coin goes.

clue.text: Disreputable hunt Alice foxed

indicators.note: foxed means baffled or confused, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fox hunt organised by someone called Alice is not quite respectable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foxed' rearranges HUNT ALICE; the fox hunt in the surface hides that it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Conduct lacking moral principle is not reputable.

clue.text: Wanderer on the sea-lanes

definitions.meaning: a vagrant who roams from place to place
a cargo ship with no fixed route, picking up trade where it can, is a ___ steamer

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a vagrant roamer and also a merchant ship trading on no regular schedule.

clue.text: Weedy growths — so I was told, anyhow

indicators.note: anyhow means in a careless, disordered way, so the letters are thrown together afresh

explanation.surface: Someone passes on, with doubt, a report of weeds springing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyhow' rearranges I WAS TOLD; 'so' is a link. The phrase also recalls the youthful 'sowing' of these.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild cereal grass of this name grows as a weed among crops.

clue.text: Lack of skill splashing paint on a Tyneside vessel

indicators.note: splashing paint about leaves its letters scattered in a new order

parts.note: NE stands for north-east England, where Tyneside is

explanation.surface: A clumsy decorator spills paint over a boat on the Tyne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splashing' rearranges PAINT into INAPT; Tyneside (around Newcastle) is in the North East, NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unsuited or clumsy at a task is a want of aptitude.

clue.text: Crossbars in the garden for training

definitions.text: Crossbars in the garden for training

parts.words: Crossbars in the garden for training
parts.note: a lattice of crossing strips fixed to a wall so climbing plants can be trained up it

explanation.surface: Sounds like gym equipment set up outdoors for exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Training' suggests athletics, but gardeners train climbing plants along a lattice.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice framework of crossed slats supports climbing plants as they are guided upward.

clue.text: Taught to deduce at random

indicators.note: random means without order, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Learning presented as a matter of guessing at random.
explanation.walkthrough: 'random' rearranges DEDUCE AT; 'to' is a link, and 'at' from the phrase 'at random' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone schooled has been instructed.

clue.text: Providing confidence at a premium, maybe

definitions.meaning: taking out life cover, for which a premium is paid

explanation.definitionFit: The word means reassuring, and also insuring a life against payment of a premium.

clue.text: Large number I employ on the female side

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
to staff a business is to employ people in it

explanation.surface: A big workforce hired by someone, mostly women.
explanation.walkthrough: D, the Roman 500, is a crossword 'large number'. The answer's 'side' is the mother's side of a family, named after the spinner's rod.
explanation.definitionFit: The ___ side of a family is the maternal line, from the spindle once used by women spinners.

clue.text: See 4
See 14
Flowers Doris arranged around a place of worship

indicators.note: around puts the shuffled letters on either side of the next piece
arranged means set out in a new order, as with flowers

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Doris sets up a floral display in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges DORIS into ORIDS, and 'around' puts that round CH.
explanation.definitionFit: These are showy flowering plants, often exotic.

clue.text: Squirrel-like creature always at the double

indicators.note: at the double means the piece is given twice over

parts.note: aye is an old word for always or ever

explanation.surface: A squirrel forever rushing about quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: AYE (rhyming with 'day') is poetic for 'always'; 'at the double' usually means quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: This Madagascan lemur with bushy tail and long fingers resembles a squirrel.

clue.text: Suit for a suitor?

parts.note: the card suit with the emblem of love, apt for one courting

explanation.surface: Asks what clothing a man courting should wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' seems to be clothing, but it is a card suit: the one whose emblem stands for love.
explanation.definitionFit: The red card suit bears the symbol of love, apt for a wooer.

clue.text: See 10
Heady fashion at Royal Ascot?

parts.note: a lively, risque manner, with a hint of the horse racing and the hats at the famous meeting

explanation.surface: Asks about the exciting outfits worn at a smart race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Ascot is a prestigious English horse-race meeting famous for elaborate hats; the first word of the answer is also 'of racing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively, spirited manner of writing or dress is called this, with racing implied at the racecourse.

clue.text: Capitally Emma is ahead of us and it's all up. Oh what a girl!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole run is read backwards
ahead of puts one piece before the other
capitally means take the capital letter, the first of the name

explanation.surface: A gushing song lyric about Emma leading the way when everything is over.
explanation.walkthrough: E (from 'Capitally Emma'), IS and US make EISUS; 'it's all up' turns the whole run up the down column. The definition quotes the song 'If You Knew ___'.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1920s song about this name has the refrain 'Oh, oh, oh, what a girl!'

clue.text: Stand right as this is said to be fit

definitions.meaning: a three-legged support for a pot or kettle by the fire

definitions.text: right as this is said to be fit
definitions.meaning: the idiom 'as right as a ___' means in perfect health

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a three-legged kitchen stand and appears in an old phrase meaning perfectly well.

clue.text: Seems the auction is going reasonably well

definitions.meaning: to look likely, as in 'it ___ to be a fine day'

definitions.text: the auction is going reasonably well
definitions.meaning: offers at a sale are decent ones

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means appears likely, and read literally says offers at a sale are reasonable.

clue.text: Assimilate the Justinian code

definitions.meaning: to take in and absorb food or ideas
the emperor Justinian's compilation of Roman law is known by this name

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to absorb food or information, and names the compendium of Roman law compiled under Justinian.

clue.text: She's sure badly but shows you your place

indicators.note: badly means poorly done, so these letters are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A woman who is no good at insurance works instead in a cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges SHE'S SURE; the apostrophe adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who guides people to their seats in a theatre or church shows them where to sit.
